request.prompt: Create a HAVENLINE World 1 authored crew upgrade concept sheet. Match the five supplied selected character references exactly in face, body proportions, hair/fur/feather pattern and scale relationships. The ONLY five actors are the referenced male survivor, referenced female survivor, referenced dog, referenced gray wolf and referenced owl. Chunky rounded stylized 3D, warm winter clothing, restrained blue metal and orange details, soft sculpted snow, clean navy studio setting. THREE large panels: two large group views across the top, a wide teamwork scene below. Top left is FRONT three-quarter, top right is the genuine opposite REAR three-quarter of the SAME outfits and gear, bottom is TEAMWORK. Every group view must show both complete humans and all three complete pets. Large readable faces, hands, feet/paws and owl wings/talons; no cropping. No extra actors, creature morphs, generic replacement faces or mixed gear versions. No numbers, costs, capacity/rate claims or implementation approval. Footer AUTHORED UPGRADE PROPOSAL. Natural animal anatomy only; no swords, guns, crossbows, human hands, boots, spiked muzzles or flight-blocking owl armor. Owls retain all visible flight feathers, open shoulder joints and clear talons. Human tools must sit in valid hands or secured sheaths and never pass through bodies. Packs do not create an inventory-capacity upgrade. The actors already work and attack; these are purposeful gear/training improvements, not new basic competence. HEADER HAVENLINE / VETERAN RESPONSE CREW. Gear design: Same source identities with substantially developed working armor: mobile blue-and-hide torso/shoulder/forearm protection on humans, larger fitted protective chest/flank panels on dog and articulated agile panels on wolf, each with reachable release fittings and no obstructed legs/jaws. Owl uses a distinct fitted lightweight aerial work rig with a protective breast/dorsal shell and compact detachable load fixture; never a heavy saddle or wing armor. Retained scarf/fur/feather language makes every actor recognizable. The owl change is an intentional flight-clear modular replacement of its old pack, not a claim the old owl lacked gear. The rear group view must match all attachments from the front; preserve free joints and reachable tool grips. Bottom teamwork scene: a coordinated defensive-response posture without enemy gore: one survivor protects a clear approach with a believable source-compatible hand tool, the other supplies or repairs a the supplied exact timber fence. Dog takes a natural interception stance beside its worker, wolf takes a distinct natural flanking posture, owl uses a believable open-wing warning/dive-ready pose. Show a useful guard-and-resupply division, not all five blindly attacking the same point. No magic, animal human weapons, extra crew or free healing. Existing animal harness/scarf/bedroll/pouches are already present in the supplied base; the upgraded work rig must be visually more useful/protective, not a generic light harness that strips the animal down. Preserve body identity while making the declared modular changes. Use only the supplied selected work object and current resource references in the scene.
